clue.text: A well-connected operator can take a girl's breath away

parts.note: breath is wind, as in being short of wind after running
a lass is a girl, and the possessive simply ties her to the breath

explanation.surface: A smooth charmer at a party can leave a young woman breathless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-connected' looks like social standing, but the operator is literally connected to a well: it is the winch that hauls up the bucket.
explanation.definitionFit: A winch with a crank and rope is fixed over a well to raise water, so it is the device worked at a well.

clue.text: Allow a pitiful thought for the imprisoned deer

indicators.note: imprisoned means the deer is shut up within the words allow a pitiful

explanation.surface: Feeling pity for a captive deer.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is held within 'alloW A PITIful', the imprisoned run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This large North American elk is a species of deer.

clue.text: Not for Tom, Harry nor anyone else that's blond perhaps ?

annotationWithheld.why: 'Not for Tom, Harry nor anyone else that's blond perhaps ?' (6): the only reading is NOR + DIC(K), with Dick the unnamed member of 'Tom, Dick and Harry' and its last letter dropped by no clue word, so no honest parse exists
annotationWithheld.clue: Not for Tom, Harry nor anyone else that's blond perhaps ?

clue.text: That idle lizard ?

parts.note: a lounge lizard is an idle man who hangs about in fashionable places

explanation.definitionFit: An idler who lazes about is someone who lounges, and a lounge lizard is that kind of loafer.

clue.text: The first coat, say, may be good enough

definitions.text: The first coat, say, may be good enough

parts.words: The first coat, say, may be good enough
parts.note: a single coat of paint may do the job adequately without another

explanation.surface: A painter hopes the first coat will be sufficient.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes a first coat of paint that needs no second: it is adequate.
explanation.definitionFit: Good enough means adequate, acceptable and passable.

clue.text: Wordsworth had two, but, said Stephen, one belonged to a sheep!

definitions.text: Wordsworth had two, but, said Stephen, one belonged to a sheep!

parts.words: Wordsworth had two, but, said Stephen, one belonged to a sheep
parts.note: Wordsworth's sonnet begins 'Two ___ are there; one is of the sea', and J. K. Stephen's parody makes the second sound belong to 'an old half-witted sheep'

explanation.surface: A literary aside about a poet's sonnet and the parody that mocked it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue needs the poems: Wordsworth's 'Two Voices are there' and J. K. Stephen's parody, where one of the two is the sea and the other a bleating sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's sonnet speaks of two sounds of liberty, the sea's and the mountains', and Stephen turned one into a sheep's bleat.

clue.text: Nothing to eat but porridge

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing
to eat is to be at a meal

explanation.surface: With nothing else to eat but porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: O for nothing, then 'to eat' read as AT MEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is made from ground oats, the grain meal of that name.

clue.text: The Grace of God is in (Belloc)

definitions.text: The Grace of God is in (Belloc)

parts.words: The Grace of God is in (Belloc)
parts.note: the last line of Hilaire Belloc's poem about good manners, which ends with the word missing here

explanation.surface: A line of Belloc's verse with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Belloc's poem 'Courtesy' ends 'That the Grace of God is in Courtesy'; the solver fills the blank.
explanation.definitionFit: Belloc's poem on politeness and good manners ends by naming that virtue as where divine grace is found.

clue.text: Philosopher's outworn garb

explanation.surface: A thinker's old-fashioned clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Spencer was a Victorian philosopher, and a spencer is a short close-fitting jacket long out of fashion.

clue.text: They pass the time for those who follow

explanation.surface: A remark about hobbies and the people who take them up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobbies are things done to pass the time, while chasers following quarry are engaged in chases of the same name.

clue.text: He portrayed the little man's views

definitions.text: He portrayed the little man's views

parts.words: He portrayed the little man's views
parts.note: the Daily Express cartoonist whose famous figure was 'the Little Man', a bowler-hatted everyman

explanation.surface: Someone gave voice to the opinions of ordinary people.
explanation.walkthrough: Sidney Strube drew cartoons for the Daily Express from the 1910s to the 1940s; his recurring character, the Little Man in a bowler hat, stood for the ordinary British citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: This cartoonist's best-known creation was the Little Man, so he drew that character's opinions on the news.

clue.text: See water from last to first, perhaps

definitions.text: water from last to first, perhaps

explanation.surface: Look at the water flowing from end to beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: This diocese of Somerset is a bishop's see, and water runs from wells, the first, to a bath, the last, so listing them backwards names it.

clue.text: Painful results of setback about aircraft component

indicators.note: about means going round, so the setback letters surround the aircraft part

parts.note: the word set, read backwards as the clue word says, gives three letters
a wing is a component of an aircraft

explanation.surface: A setback with an aircraft part has painful consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setback' looks like a misfortune, but it is split into its parts: the word set, read back.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp sudden pains are the results felt after a strain or injury.

clue.text: Like dressing a type of tank ?

parts.note: a septic tank is the underground tank for sewage

explanation.surface: Asking what sort of tank something resembles in its dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' is a wound dressing, not salad dressing; such dressings must be sterile.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical dressing is kept sterile and free of germs, which is the sense wanted.

clue.text: One finds the B.A.'s rarely equal to a test of concentration

indicators.note: one finds the letters of these words, set out again in a new order

parts.note: B.A. is written as its letters with the S kept

explanation.surface: Graduates with a Bachelor of Arts are seldom up to a test of focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concentration' means alcohol in the blood, not mental focus. THE, BAS and RARELY together hold the twelve letters, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadside device a motorist blows into measures the alcohol level in the breath.

clue.text: For the rest, it's a plant !

definitions.text: For the rest, it's a plant !

parts.words: For the rest, it's a plant
parts.note: a bed of straw is for resting on, and the same pair of words names a wild flower

explanation.surface: Something used for resting turns out to be a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as BED STRAW it is something to lie on; as one word it is a meadow plant, once used to stuff mattresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Galium, a slender wild flower once dried to stuff mattresses, is the plant named.

clue.text: No run on this creature's account, usually

definitions.text: No run on this creature's account, usually

parts.words: No run on this creature's account, usually
parts.note: no run is a duck in cricket and an account is a bill, so the creature has a duck bill

explanation.surface: A cricket remark about a batsman's score.
explanation.walkthrough: A score of nothing in cricket is a duck, and a bill is an account: the creature is the duck-billed one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian egg-laying mammal is known for its broad flat beak like a waterfowl's.

clue.text: Putting us wise with points to shedding weight ?

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north
lightening a load means making it lose weight

explanation.surface: Advice on losing weight that also teaches us something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' are compass points, E and N, placed before LIGHTENING.
explanation.definitionFit: Informing someone makes them wiser, which is putting them wise.

clue.text: To the Turks perhaps a G.I. or us Christians

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words could be arranged another way

parts.note: G.I. is an American soldier, written as its two letters

explanation.surface: To the Turks, an American soldier or we ourselves count as Christians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To the Turks' qualifies the definition: the word is Turkish usage for non-Muslims. A, GI, OR and US are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In Turkish usage this term labelled non-Muslims, especially Christians, as unbelievers.

clue.text: Nasty racket about an award of distinction

indicators.note: about means the word for racket goes round the award

parts.note: a racket is a loud noise
OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour of distinction

explanation.surface: An unpleasant din surrounding the presentation of an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour; NOISE goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Offensive and unpleasant, especially in smell, is what nasty can mean here.

clue.text: The centre court at Rome

parts.note: the central open courtyard of an ancient Roman house

explanation.surface: A tennis venue in the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre court' suggests tennis, but it is the open hall at the middle of a Roman house.
explanation.definitionFit: The open central hall of a Roman dwelling is the courtyard meant.

clue.text: Get the three first in the race for a double

definitions.text: Get the three first in the race for a double

parts.words: Get the three first in the race for a double
parts.note: putting three before the race makes the three-___ race, run in pairs with two legs tied together

explanation.surface: Advice to finish in the top three of a race to win a double bet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a three-legged race two runners are tied together, a double act, and the word missing between 'three' and 'race' is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase three-legged race needs this word with legs, describing pairs of runners bound together.

clue.text: Hair-do just right for a sunny day ?

parts.note: a set is a hair-do, as in a shampoo and set
fair means just, right and even-handed

explanation.surface: A new hair-do is perfect for a bright day out.
explanation.walkthrough: The barometer's dial marks the reading for settled weather with this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The barometer reading for settled fine weather is the phrase wanted, so it suits a sunny day.

clue.text: Street musicians' wind-raiser?

parts.note: buskers play a cheap tin pipe, and sailors once believed that blowing one would raise a wind

explanation.surface: A question about what a busker uses to work up some air.
explanation.walkthrough: Buskers play the tin version, and an old sailors' superstition held that the sound summoned a wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The penny pipe of street players is also the instrument sailors blew to call up a breeze.

clue.text: About the ad., put it in again

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a plug is an advertisement, a free mention

explanation.surface: Talking about the advertisement, someone says to run it once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put it in again' reads as reinserting a plug, defining the word built from RE and PLUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconnecting an appliance to a socket is inserting its pin connector once more.

clue.text: The pottery sounds depressed, but is really flourishing

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word for depressed is spelt as heard, not as written

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling depressed
Ming is fine Chinese porcelain of the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: The pottery shop seems gloomy, yet the business is doing very well.
explanation.walkthrough: BLUE MING spoken gives the answer; 'sounds' turns BLUE into BLOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant in flower is thriving, so it describes something flourishing.

clue.text: Most sage is of use when stew is made

indicators.note: when stew is made its ingredients are mixed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The wisest course is to be useful while the stew is being cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made' is the anagram signal: STEW and IS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage means wise, so the most sage is the wisest of all.

clue.text: Meets in the river to return such favours

indicators.note: to return means the whole assembled run is read backwards
in means the word meets is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: Meeting at the river in order to repay kind gestures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To return' turns the whole assembly round. Old business letters thanked a client for 'your esteemed favour', a stock phrase for a letter received.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal correspondence spoke of a correspondent's valued letters, a polite way of praising them.
